The deploy at 23:26:00Z lines up closely with the failure onset, and since the source repo is k8s-configs, this looks like a config-induced-failure. I'm trying to verify by checking whether process_start_time_seconds stayed constant across the window, which means computing the epoch timestamp to confirm the exact deploy time against 2026-09-22.

Working through the epoch math, I find the process actually started around 11:29:23Z, roughly 12 hours before the deploy — meaning the pod never restarted at deploy time. That undercuts the config-induced-failure theory, since a genuine deploy typically triggers a restart. Memory stays flat at 461MB (21% of limit) ruling out a leak, traffic is flat or slightly declining, but latency climbs steadily with timeout errors — pointing more toward an upstream dependency failure, though nothing in the logs explicitly names an upstream service. I've already checked the wider log window and found nothing new, so I'm weighing config-induced-failure, upstream-dependency-failure, and bad-deployment as the main candidates, with the exact timing coincidence still nagging at me.

Given the deploy timing coincides almost precisely with onset and the repo is k8s-configs, I'll lean toward config-induced-failure with roughly 0.5-0.55 confidence, noting the from/to states are unknown so I'll just cite the revision as subject. I also note the metrics window opens already at baseline levels around 23:26, so onset is really a lower bound rather than a precise marker. I'll finalize my answer now.
